summary.intent: Run the GSD milestone manager to discuss Phase 42 (API unpin integrity) and lock implementation decisions for the missing ownership check and unpin quota bugs, then start Phase 43.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 discussion completed with all gray areas resolved and decisions committed to 42-CONTEXT.md and 42-DISCUSSION-LOG.md. Phase 43 discussion was initialized before the session ended.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) is authenticated by JwtAuthGuard only — it never reads req.user and passes any CID string directly to Kubo pin/rm, making it a wide-open cross-tenant data-destruction surface for any account holder.

Kubo v0.40 runs with the 'server' profile on staging (docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72) with swarm port 4001 exposed publicly — the server profile keeps full public DHT participation, so all pinned CIDs are broadcast as provider records and harvestable by DHT crawlers.
All current callers silently swallow unpin errors: web hook uses .catch(logger.warn), FUSE uses let _ = — nothing breaks functionally on a failed unpin today.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without calling unpin (confirmed at shared-write.ts:450), so there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path in the system.
Kubo API port 5001 is loopback-only since Phase 29; the NestJS API endpoint is the only external path in.
BYO-IPFS capability has its own unpin path (provider.unpin injection) but it is not wired into delete flows.

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm on a CID that may be content-addressed-deduped across users — no ownership check.
Kubo v0.40 configured with 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (tcp+udp), meaning all pinned CIDs are advertised to the public IPFS DHT.
Unpin errors are caught and logged as warnings only — clients do not read or act on unpin response status codes.

workflow: The GSD discuss-phase workflow locks decisions into a CONTEXT.md checkpoint JSON before writing the final CONTEXT.md, enabling partial recovery if the session is interrupted.
Presenting option menus when the user asked a direct factual question caused friction — the discuss workflow should answer directly before offering choices.
Advisory xact lock on hash(cid) in Postgres is the preferred pattern for closing concurrent-delete races on deduped content, rather than relying on a reconciliation job.
